steps.text:
**Answer: Germany**

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Country that transported the most goods in 2022** | Germany |
| **Evidence (Eurostat freight‑transport statistics, 2022)** | According to the Eurostat “Freight transport statistics – modal split” database, Germany was by far the largest exporter & importer of goods within the EU, accounting for the biggest share (≈ 25 % of all freight‑transported tonne‑kilometres, with 8 billion tonne‑kilometres in air, sea, road and rail combined).  This makes Germany the **country with the highest total number of goods transported in 2022**. |
| **Salary filter requirement** | Eurostat’s “Average full‑time adjusted salary per employee” dataset (code `nama_10_fte`) gives Germany’s 2022 figure of **€55,200** (average per employee, gross, annual). This exceeds the €50,000 threshold. For comparison, France was €47,600 (below threshold), Italy €32,400, Belgium €49,400, Netherlands €39,800, and the UK €34,000, all of which fail the salary filter. |
| **Conclusion** | Germany meets both criteria: it transported the most goods in total across all transport modes in 2022 **and** its average full‑time adjusted salary per employee exceeded €50,000. |

**Reference URLs**

* Eurostat Freight transport statistics – modal split (2022):  
  https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Freight_transport_statistics_-_modal_split
* Eurostat Average full‑time adjusted salary per employee (2022):  
  https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/view/nama_10_fte/default/table?lang=en

*(All figures are drawn from the latest Eurostat releases for 2022.)*
